all_rows.statement: The system gives AI agents long-term memory: an event log of everything said and done, projections that make it searchable, and a per-turn context block plus pull tools that put the relevant part in front of the model. The targets are the user's words "massive long term context" and "extreme recall

The deliverable is a client deployment for an Elastic customer, "not just for my harness/internal use" (user, WAL w55d0a51fc1f). The concrete shape is main's choice, not the user's: a standalone memory core on the client's Postgres and Elasticsearch, with Agent Builder and client model providers beh

Subscription Claude and Codex CLIs are development adapters only, behind the same model port. The user asked for adapters "so we can test and use it with our subscription based claude/codex instances" (WAL wd8b56ed99b8). Whether they may sit behind Elasticsearch's inference API is an open ask (WAL w

Ideas enter the design only from LEDGER's "Held" table, at the evidence class shown there; failed ideas stay recorded with the reason. Source: the user's "incorporate into designs whatever proves to work, keep track of what doesnt".
The Postgres log is the only source of truth. Elasticsearch holds rebuildable projections only. The durable engine holds ids and cursors only.

all_rows.statement: A stale writer is refused by the store, not by caller discipline. The lease epoch travels in the write and is checked under lock in Postgres, and by a per-epoch Elasticsearch write alias with require_alias.
all_rows.evidence: [REVIEWED] RV-WP N3, N3S_projector, N5, N8 SUPPORTED; limit: holds for honest stale writers that present their own token (RV-WP F3)

all_rows.statement: Hybrid retrieval alone can serve as the memory. It did not: whole-pool recall in section 1 (exploratory, pilot). So: retrieval is one input to context, with a current-state table and an analyst tier above it.

Automatic supersession links can act as a filter. They did not: link recall 10 of 16. So: supersession labels are advisory, never a filter, and the user chose "Dated facts, links optional" (WAL w0fdb289edad).

Owner-reported passes hold without independent review. They did not: the first adversarial reviews confirmed 12 challenged material findings in the adapters and 12 in the write-path skeleton. So: no pass counts until an independent review confirms it.

The proof rules in gotchas/PROOF-RULES.md apply to every experiment: a failing control above a stated sensitivity floor, witness counts, pre-committed thresholds, per-item artifacts and an environment fingerprint.
Events are appended to a Postgres table with a per-stream sequence and a hash chain (seq, prev_hash).
16 concurrent live writers produced a gapless sequence. This says nothing about clock skew, cross-host ordering or a stale writer.
all_rows.evidence: [REVIEWED] RV-SYS "recomputed and matching" (C7); limit from GOT CORRECTIONS

all_rows.statement: A zombie session that lost its lease is quarantined: 20 of 20 zombie appends were stored as unadopted in both stall positions, the chain verified and nothing was projected.

Takeover always completes after a zombie loses its lease. It does not: a zombie that stalls after its insert while holding its lease row blocks takeover indefinitely, because `acquire` sets no lock timeout.
The projector cursor reads only rows whose transaction committed below the cluster-wide snapshot xmin, so a late commit is never skipped.
all_rows.evidence: [REVIEWED] RV-WP "Late commit (row 23)": Postgres half SUPPORTED; limit: any long transaction anywhere in the cluster stalls projection for every tenant

all_rows.statement: While one transaction is held open for 12 s, a reader still finds a new event through the log tail, and projection catches up 0.73 s after the commit. The run has no failing control and covers one database, not a cluster-wide stall across databases.
The signed chain head is anchored outside the database with a promotion epoch, and projection stops at the replication-confirmed LSN.
The hash chain covers stored bytes, so an upcaster bug changes what an old event means without breaking verification. Old-event golden replays are needed.
A memory append must never fail silently.
Secret and credential scanning runs before append, including encoded variants.

Index names are chosen by an immutable field (plain index, op_type=create, deterministic routing), not by a rolled alias or a data stream. On a data stream the same _id is accepted again after a rollover.
all_rows.evidence: [REVIEWED] RV-ES writes E3a, E3b, E3c and alternatives REPRODUCED

all_rows.statement: Conditional writes with if_seq_no and if_primary_term give exactly one winner. `_bulk` has no cross-item atomicity, so per-item statuses must be read.
all_rows.evidence: [REVIEWED] RV-ES writes E2 REPRODUCED; E8d PARTLY (HTTP 200 with an item-level 400)

all_rows.statement: Search visibility after a write takes about one second at the default refresh (p50 1,001 ms over 200 writes on a loaded host). Recent events are read from the log tail, not from search.
Read-after-write through the tail scan held for 100 of 100 reads, and 600 events written during a projector pause were all found.

Every projection is rebuildable from the log. A blue/green rebuild showed no mixed view, but its control never produced a mixed view, so that half is unproven. A dropped bucket stays missing until an explicit repair.

all_rows.statement: The embedder identity (model, revision, prefix, normalisation) and the vector index options are part of each generation's name and _meta. Inference endpoint ids are immutable per revision.

Erasure is per-subject key destruction in a separate key store, plus removal of derived rows through input-set provenance, then a rebuild of every registered index family.
Phase 1 bumps the lease first, in one transaction with the tombstones and the job row. Writers racing phase 1 leave no residue.

Model-facing ids are opaque, after real gold session ids were all found to begin with `answer_`. A re-test with opaque ids changed no outcome (9 of 10, 16 of 16); the dev2 gate-3 answers were not re-run.

all_rows.statement: Decisions in the systems skeleton are version-bound and idempotent. They were not: a stale acceptance overwrote a newer user decision, a replay re-applied a reverted change, and a retried decision dropped a pending change.
In the rebuilt write path, decisions use compare-and-set: the stale-acceptance, replay and retry cases hold 10 of 10.
all_rows.evidence: [REVIEWED] RV-WP N7 PARTLY: cases (a), (b) and (c) hold

all_rows.statement: In the rebuilt write path, decisions are bound to the approval itself. They are not yet: the version comes from the caller, heads are per session, one typed message can authorise unlimited decisions, and an idempotency key reused with different content returns "duplicate".
Whether decision items are per session or tenant-wide is a product choice (OPEN-QUESTIONS J1 implies tenant-wide).

Every step and every injected block records the definition version and watermark it used (the acted-on version). The generated-scenario oracle shares the fold's version-blind rule, so its result is not independent.
Only an authorised human-typed decision flips state; two agents cannot approve each other; a revoked principal's pending decision is invalidated.
The current-state table is a fold of events, checked by an oracle, following agent-fabric's reducer discipline.
Lower trust never supersedes higher across sibling scopes.

all_rows.statement: Records are framed with a per-turn random delimiter, one JSON-escaped record per line, so a stored `</memory>` or `SYSTEM:` line cannot forge the framing.
The primary budget is 4,000 tokens, chosen on the pilot after the first selection rule failed to fire.

Gold presence grows with budget. At the whole pool, at least one gold session is present for 0.53, 0.62, 0.71 and 0.79 of questions at 4,000, 8,000, 16,000 and 32,000 tokens. No claim about context rot follows.
Injection and trimming keep tool-call and tool-result pairing valid (in the Anthropic Messages API a tool_result must follow its tool_use).
Compaction is recorded as an event that ends in-context status and forces the state card and manifest to regenerate. A resumed turn re-sends the sealed block verbatim plus a labelled delta.
Every item presented as current carries its source event and a checked-through watermark, and a bounded scan after that watermark surfaces challengers.

all_rows.statement: The prompt-cache cost of a regenerated block is unmeasured.
Agent Builder injection must use the same randomised framing; a Kibana template that uses the raw `<memory>` format is superseded.
Retrieval is BM25 plus dense vectors, fused client-side with RRF (rank constant 60) on the Basic required path. The rank constant was selected on the pilot.

Recall falls monotonically with pool size. RRF session recall@10 is 0.968, 0.859, 0.684 and 0.4754 at H0 to H3. At H3 plain BM25 (0.494) and linear fusion (0.492) score slightly higher than RRF, and dense alone 0.345.
23 of 94 pilot questions are low-overlap at the whole pool (gold round ranked worse than 100 on both BM25 and dense). The cut was chosen after the counts were seen.
Session length alone separates gold from other sessions (AUROC 0.687 against a null of 0.448 to 0.547), so this benchmark carries a length shortcut.
A cross-encoder rerank (top 20) sits after fusion. It cost about 64 s per question at top 50 on CPU.
The rerank beats plain RRF at the whole pool: session recall@10 +0.059 [+0.016, +0.113], on 78 of 94 questions while the pooled rerank run was still in progress.
Concept links boost and never filter.

Pull tools for the model: recall(query, as_of), open_event(id), query_facts(subject, predicate, as_of), timeline(entity). A Claude Code headless session used them over MCP to answer a current-versus-past question.
As-of filtering is only a safety rule on this benchmark: the day rule removes 0 gold sessions, so it cannot change a ranking here.
Standing queries (percolator) are lexical only: Elasticsearch rejects vector queries inside the percolator.

An analyst run is keyed on (logical session, step, manifest hash), draws on the originating step's budget reservation and is killed when it stops making progress.
Findings follow a fixed schema with an explicit "nothing relevant" outcome that suppresses injection.
Analysts read untrusted transcripts and must never relay a planted instruction.
Policy is re-evaluated at delivery, not only at enqueue.
Reviewer and click-tester sessions never receive items whose origin is in the author set.

Labels (tenant, access list, classification, region, handling) travel with every event; a derived row's access is the intersection of its inputs' access and its restrictions the union.
Identity and tenant attributes cannot be overwritten by derived attributes; a non-boolean or erroring evaluation denies.
A refusal or a policy denial is never retried on another model without a recorded, authorised route.
The policy point refuses subscription adapters in any production profile.
Which concrete policies apply (regions, classifications, approved models) is the client's or the user's choice; the system ships with none assumed.
